PullRequest.Title: ci: fix JSON integration test build setup
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Fix two coupled integration-test setup problems introduced by #336754. [Azure build 475244 (20260919.7)](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=475244) fails on Windows, Linux, and macOS at the new standalone JSON suite.

1. **Compile the JSON client tests.** The runner launches `extensions/json-language-features/client/out/test/index.js`, but the explicit build lists compile only the server. Add the existing `compile-extension:json-language-features-client` task alongside the server in all eight relevant lists: the three platform product-test templates, three PR workflows, and both OS branches of the shared flaky-test build.
2. **Honor product-build output in the JSON fixture.** Product `core-ci` emits shared core modules into `out-build`; PR/development transpilation emits `out`. The JSON fixture hardcoded `out/vs/base/common/uri.js`, and neither shared runner passed `--build` to the standalone suite. Forward that flag in both shell and batch runners and use the existing test-runner `out-build`/`out` convention. Update help and the integration-test guide.

No product runtime behavior, dependency manifests, existing suites, or error handling is bypassed. Output selection is explicit, not a filesystem fallback.

## Validation

The follow-up was first reproduced with genuine `out-build` modules and no development `out` URI: `./scripts/test-integration.sh --suite json --build --tfs 'Integration Tests'` failed with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for the hardcoded `out/vs/base/common/uri.js`. This exposed the gap in the initial development-only validation.

After the fix, the actual shared runner passed on macOS arm64 with repository-managed Electron 43.6.0 / Node 24.20.0 and `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1`:

| Output layout | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `out-build` only; development URI absent | `./scripts/test-integration.sh --suite json --build --tfs 'Integration Tests'` | 39 passed |
| `out` only; build URI absent | `./scripts/test-integration.sh --suite json` | 39 passed |
| `out-build` only; build flag first and grep applied | `./scripts/test-integration.sh --build --suite json --grep 'JSON schema URL matching'` | 9 passed |

- Separate JUnit reports confirm the nonzero test counts and zero failures. Opposite output paths were asserted absent before and after each run. Both deliberately wrong-mode controls failed instead of falling back to the other output tree.
- The unchanged client compile task passed with zero errors via `npm run gulp -- --gulpfile build/gulpfile.extensions.ts --cwd . compile-extension:json-language-features-client`. Verified genuine emitted tests, helpers, and production modules.
- Both core fixture layouts were emitted from the seven real URI source dependencies using the repository's unchanged `build/next/transpile.ts` `transpileFile` helper, the same helper used by product transpilation.
- All seven changed YAML files parse; all eight compile commands passed Bash/native PowerShell syntax checks. The shell runner passes `bash -n` and its help command. Normal pre-commit hygiene and signing were preserved for both commits.

**Limits:** This fresh worktree used isolated dependency closures from repository lockfiles. The default root Gulp entrypoint eagerly reads unrelated, unrestored Copilot SDK metadata, so the existing extension gulpfile was used directly; a full `core-ci` build was not run. Windows batch/Linux execution and an official pipeline run remain unverified. No Azure build was queued or rerun.

Scenarios.Scenario: Source-based PR integration jobs on macOS, Linux, and Windows compile extensions and run the full Electron integration suite, including standalone JSON tests.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The extension build step must complete before the Electron integration step. The added JSON client compile is therefore on the CI critical path, but it produces the previously missing test entrypoint required by the JSON suite.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compile the JSON language-features client with the repository compiler task.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One added compiler task in each applicable platform job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The jobs compiled only the JSON server, then attempted to run the missing client/out/test/index.js.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds bounded compile CPU and filesystem work before integration tests, but that output is required for the JSON runner that the same job executes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: scripts/test-integration.sh and scripts/test-integration.bat JSON suite blocks
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch the standalone JSON suite through node-electron.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One launch per full integration run, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same node-electron process was launched without the build-layout selector.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains on the integration-test critical path; forwarding --build does not add another launch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the shared URI module from out or out-build.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Called by test fixture creation; Node's module cache serves repeated loads within the process. The diff only selects the existing output tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same module was loaded only from out, which failed when product CI provided only out-build.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A synchronous module load already occurred on fixture setup; selecting out-build does not add an extra read.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One JSON client TypeScript project per enabled platform job; it does not scale with test count, schemas, or repository history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single existing Gulp invocation receives one additional named compile task alongside the other extension tasks. There is no changed loop or per-test scheduling, so cardinality is bounded to one compile task per platform job.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The compile task explicitly removes client/out and its tsbuildinfo before spawning the compiler, so each CI job is cold by design. No new cache key or miss retry is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: task implementation, workflow ordering, and JSON runner call path are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact compiler duration and peak memory vary by agent, but work is one bounded project compile and is necessary for the suite; there is no evidence of material excess work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added bounded compile cost enables an already-scheduled suite rather than introducing avoidable repeated or scaling work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Product-build Electron integration jobs run against out-build on macOS, Linux, and Windows.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The unconditional integration-extension build precedes the conditionally enabled Electron integration run. In current CI product configurations Electron tests are enabled, and the added client output is consumed by the JSON suite through --build.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One added compiler task per product test job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the JSON server was compiled, leaving the standalone client tests unavailable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before Electron integration tests and creates client/out test files used by the suite.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One underlying module initialization per JSON test process due to require caching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The fixture attempted the out path and failed in product-build layouts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required during fixture setup; the diff redirects the existing load rather than adding a second load or fallback probe.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One compile per product platform/architecture job and one JSON process per integration run.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The added task joins the existing multi-task Gulp invocation; no per-file or per-test subprocess loop is introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Compilation is cold because the task cleans output and tsbuildinfo. URI module loading is warm after Node's first require in the JSON test process.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for current product CI call paths; moderate for every possible external template instantiation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Template parameters can support non-Electron modes, but the inspected CI product invocations enable Electron tests; even in another mode the incremental cost is one bounded compile, not a high-confidence material regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added compiler work has fixed cardinality and is directly consumed on the configured product integration path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Flaky integration pipelines compile once, archive the workspace, and run multiple Electron integration iterations from the artifact.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The JSON client compilation and workspace archive complete before downstream integration jobs. Each iteration then runs the JSON suite from the extracted artifact without recompiling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compile the JSON client in the shared flaky build job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One added compiler task per selected platform build, independent of iteration count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The shared workspace omitted the compiled client tests, so downstream JSON runs could not start.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks artifact creation once, then avoids recompilation in every downstream integration iteration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: build/azure-pipelines/common/product-smoke-flaky-build.yml archiveWorkspaceSteps transitively after Build integration tests
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Include client/out in the existing workspace archive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One archive per platform build; all iterations reuse it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same archive/upload/download path existed but lacked client/out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds only the bounded emitted client files to an archive operation that already transfers the workspace.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish and download the existing workspace artifact for downstream integration jobs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One publish and one download per downstream job under existing pipeline structure; the diff only adds bounded client output bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same artifact transfers occurred with a slightly smaller workspace that could not run JSON client tests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Artifact transfer remains required before iterations; no new transfer is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One compile and one inclusion in the workspace artifact per platform build; test iterations reuse that artifact, so compile work does not scale with iteration count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Compilation occurs once in the shared build job. Downstream iterations may execute according to pipeline job scheduling, but the diff does not create additional compile concurrency per iteration.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The compile itself is cold. The resulting client/out files are effectively cached in the workspace artifact and reused by all iterations; each test process has its own Node module cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: shared-build comments, archive ordering, and iteration runners directly establish reuse.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact emitted byte size and archive-time delta are not measured, but the project is bounded and archived once; no realistic unbounded or iteration-multiplied mechanism is present.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The architecture coalesces compilation before fan-out and reuses the output across flaky iterations.

Scenarios.Scenario: Local or CI invocation of the standalone JSON suite with --build selects product core modules.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Argument parsing occurs before the existing node-electron launch; fixture setup then chooses out-build and loads URI before tests execute.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the JSON test index under node-electron with --build.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing process launch per selected JSON suite.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same test process launched without access to the build-layout signal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The added argument only controls module path selection and does not add a process or await.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Require URI from the chosen core output directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One module initialization per process after Node cache coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Necessary fixture setup, with no additional fallback filesystem access.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Argument inspection scales with the very small process argv array; path construction is constant-size. Repeated fixture setup reuses Node's module cache.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One JSON test process; the diff adds no parallel operation, queue, or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The selected URI module is cold on first require and warm thereafter in the process. There is no fallback probing or negative-cache retry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: direct argument flow and fixture code establish the complete path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Negligible path-selection overhead is structurally clear; no benchmark is needed to reject a material regression.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 11 changed files and traced CI compilation, standalone JSON execution, module loading, and flaky artifact reuse. The PR adds bounded, necessary build work and layout selection without repeated boundary calls, unbounded retention, cache churn, or new fan-out. No performance findings or regression-fix learning records were warranted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
